question: Does prompt caching actually fire on long sessions, and what does it save on glm-5.3-flash vs deepseek-v4.1-flash?
method: Two identical 7-turn named sessions (e07a, e07b) on z-ai/glm-5.3-flash --reasoning low, provider nous. Turn 1 loads a ~12.8k-word synthetic doc (steady prefix); turns 2-7 ask short questions against it. Per-turn tokens read from --format stream-json results. Total cost of the experiment: under $0.01.

session_a.note: turn 1 fully cold (28,379 fresh); doc re-read as cache from turn 3 on; some turns partially cached (18% prefix-refresh drift on turns 2/5)

session_b.note: warmest run: even turn 1 hit a provider-side cache (28,352) — same doc within cache TTL from session A

cache_ratio.note: cached vs fresh input price ratios (model-prices.json ). Same session shape on deepseek would save ~85% of input cost; on glm only 21-36%.

verdict: Caching WORKS on glm-5.3-flash (steady prefix re-reads as cache, prefix-refresh drift is small) but saves little money there, because its input price is already tiny (cached only 1.56x cheaper than fresh). The session-shape win on glm is not re-sending output-heavy turns, not cheap input. On deepseek pins, the same steady-prefix discipline saves ~6.7x on input — cache hygiene matters much more there.
recommendation: No config change. For long sessions on glm: keep prefix stable and avoid re-sending big outputs; for bulk runs on deepseek pins: steady prefix layout is a real cost lever.
